reading.body:
Cognex holds 304 granted US patents, and its most recent ones are about light, not models. The five newest grants cover multispectral illumination, beam-sweeping, an illumination assembly, box-shape estimation, and symbol-reader tuning. That is the shape of a company whose edge sits in the optical and mechanical path in front of the sensor.

This matters for AI because machine vision is where computer vision has run in production the longest, and the binding constraints there have never been compute alone. A camera that cannot light a part correctly, or estimate a box's shape, fails regardless of the model behind it. Cognex's patent stream suggests the durable work is in capturing a usable image of a physical object on a moving line, which is a different problem from scaling training runs.

The data does not include revenue, customers, or any measure of whether these patents are used in shipping products. It also does not connect Cognex to data centers, power, or grid capacity, and nothing here supports that link. What it covers is a Massachusetts industrial instruments company, its SEC filing cadence through 2026, and a patent record concentrated on imaging hardware.

profile_text.body:
Cognex is a machine vision company headquartered in Natick, Massachusetts, with offices in more than 20 countries. Its cameras, sensors and software inspect and identify parts on production lines, detect defects, verify assembly and guide assembly robots, which makes it one of the longest-running commercial users of computer vision in manufacturing.

Source: Wikipedia, Cognex Corporation, retrieved 22 September 2026.
